body:
maria (eng-runtime): heads-up — ran the nightly perf sweep for kv-warmup/kernel-route. p99 jumped ~120ms at ~1.5k qps for model x-gpt-7b-quant. trace attached in S3.

ravi (eng-ml): saw that too. root cause looks like kernel selector flipped to the slower attention kernel when seqlen>1024 under certain batch shapes. repro: `perf record --call-graph`, nvprof shows membandwidth spike during KV restore.

maria (eng-runtime): repro script: ```bash
./bench --qps 1500 --seq 1200 --microbatch 8 --kv-warmup=true
```
output snippet: ```
p95: 64ms p99: 312ms
CPU wait for cudaMemcpy: 90ms spike
```

aj (product): is this customer-facing? deepa (sales) — any active deals that need strict p99? we should decide if this merits an incident or negotiated carveout. :thinking: 

deepa (sales): yes — StellarPay is in final CRO stage and asked for p95=120ms / p99<=220ms. ken (acct-stellar) was pinged, want confirmation from eng if achievable without dedicated.

ken (acct-stellar): our internal SLA target is p99<200ms. We can tolerate small maintenance windows but need a plan before GA.

ravi (eng-ml): options: 1) force faster attention kernel for that model/seqlen with heuristic override (low risk, ~5-10% throughput loss), 2) reduce microbatch from 8->4 for that tenant (improves tail but increases CPU/GPU ops -> cost up), 3) per-tenant KV pre-warm during session start (adds warmup traffic but offsets tail), 4) reserve dedicated capacity with pinned kernel path (best latency).

maria (eng-runtime): quick numbers from lab: microbatch=8 @1.5k qps => p99 312ms; microbatch=4 => p99 190ms, throughput drops ~18%. Forcing kernel yields p99 ~170ms but qps down ~12%. KV pre-warm reduces variance for repeated sessions (p99 ~200ms) but has warmup cost.

aj (product): tradeoffs sound reasonable. Proposal: offer StellarPay two options — (A) self-serve tweak: microbatch=4 + routing priority, (B) enterprise carveout: dedicated capacity + pinned kernel + KV warmup (SLA p99 200ms). Allow them to pick. We should also test forcing kernel for edge case.

deepa (sales): I'll present both options. We need implementation plan and risk notes to share.

maria (eng-runtime): immediate action items: 1) create canary config for kernel-override + microbatch=4 for tenant=stellarpay, 2) run 6-hour perf run at ramped qps, 3) add regression test to nightly to catch kernel-selector flip for seqlen 1024-1400.

ravi (eng-ml): I'll open PR with kernel-override flag and microbatch config. tagging @maria for canary infra.

maria (eng-runtime): started canary: deploy-bot: "canary: kernel-override enabled for tenant=stellarpay on pool-7 (3 instances)" :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary metrics streaming to dashboard -> https://internal.redwood/dash/1934567890

ken (acct-stellar): thanks — please keep our PM looped. We'll validate on our side once you flip the canary.

aj (product): once canary completes, we'll do a joint validation call with StellarPay and finalize the contract language (carveout vs default). aim: decision by EOD tomorrow.

maria (eng-runtime): noted. if canary fails we'll fallback plan: auto-roll to pinned-kernel only for dedicated customers and add cost estimate.

deepa (sales): great. I'll prep two slide bullets for the call.

ravi (eng-ml): PR link when ready: https://git.internal/redwood/eng-runtime/pulls/614 (WIP)

maria (eng-runtime): adding nightly regression: `tests/perf/regress/kv_kernelflip.py` — will alert #eng-runtime when selector changes behavior.

ken (acct-stellar): :thumbsup: good to see a plan.

maria (eng-runtime): thanks all — will post canary perf summary in this thread after 6h.

(threads like this are short; follow-ups will be separate threads if we escalate.)
